items.title: ロシアの邦人記者拘束、自民から対応強化求める声　高市首相はスパイ行為否定
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Tamiyuki Kihara　Yoshifumi Takemoto

[東京 １５日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Tamiyuki Kihara　Yoshifumi Takemoto

[東京 １５日 ロイター] - ロシア当局が北海道新聞の日本人記者をスパイ容疑で拘束した問題で、自民党内から政府の対応強化を求める声が上がっている。１５日の党会合で、外務省はロシア側から拘束についての正式な報告がないと説明。高市早苗首相は同日、記者団にロシアでのスパイ活動を否定し、邦人保護に注力する考えを示した。

自民は１５日朝、外交部会と外交調査会の合同会議を開いた。出席者によると、複数の議員からロシアに対して記者の解放を強く求めるべきとの声が上がった。閣僚経験のある衆院議員は政府がスパイ容疑について明確に否定していない点を問題視し、「あり得ない対応だ。まずは容疑を否定し、記者の解放を求めるべきだ」と語った。

会議の中で、外務省は現在も記者との領事面会が実現しておらず、いまだにウィーン条約に基づく外国人拘束時の通知義務である「領事通報」が行われていない、と説明したという。前出の衆院議員は「ロシアが対日圧力のために拘束した可能性がある。政府は強い態度で臨まなければならない」と述べた。

同じく会議に出席した別の閣僚経験者は、日本の国益も考えながらバランスよく外交を展開する必要があるとしつつ、「もはやきれいごとの時代ではない」と語気を強めた。

高市氏は同日、首相官邸で記者団の取材に応じた。その中で「外務省がいま、一生懸命動いて、ロシア当局に対して申し入れもし、面会も含めて求めている」と説明。記者から、日本政府はロシアでスパイ活動をしているのかと問われると「そのような事実はございません」と否定し、「それぞれ国内法も違う。（ロシアが）容疑と言っていることの詳細もまだ分からないが、日本の立場をしっかりと伝えていく」と語った。

これに先立ち、木原稔官房長官は同日午前の記者会見で、１４日に駐日ロシア大使を外務省に呼び、情報提供や人道的な配慮を求めたとした。その上で、「日本政府として何らの説明を受けていない中で、ロシア側が邦人を拘束し、それについての発信を一方的に行っていることに強く抗議をした」とも明らかにした。

記者の健康状態などの確認はできておらず、木原氏は引き続きロシア側に申し入れなど必要な対応をとる、とも述べた。

ロシア連邦保安局（ＦＳＢ）は１３日、記者をスパイ容疑で拘束したと発表した。ロシア外務省は、日本政府が記者をスパイ活動に利用しているのは遺憾だと表明。ＦＳＢがウェブサイトに掲載した声明によると、記者はロシア出国を予定していた日の前日に極東サハリン州で拘束された。具体的な拘束日は明らかにしていないが、今回の拘束が日ロ関係に新たな影を落とす、としている。

（鬼原民幸、竹本能文　編集：橋本浩）

items.summary: Pakistan has recorded the worst performance in South Asia in the 2026 Global Hunger Index, highlighting the country’s deepening food insecurity amid economic instability, soaring food prices, ...
items.body:
Pakistan ranks worst in South Asia on 2026 Global Hunger Index as food insecurity deepens Pakistan has recorded the worst performance in South Asia in the 2026 Global Hunger Index, highlighting the country’s deepening food insecurity amid economic instability, soaring food prices, climate-related disasters and international conflicts, as reported by Dawn.
ANI | Updated: 15-10-2026 17:01 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 17:01 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pakistan has recorded the worst performance in South Asia in the 2026 Global Hunger Index, highlighting the country’s deepening food insecurity amid economic instability, soaring food prices, climate-related disasters and international conflicts, as reported by Dawn. According to Dawn, the report, under the theme “No Security Without Food Security”, was jointly prepared by Welthungerhilfe, the Institute for International Law of Peace and Armed Conflict at Ruhr University Bochum, and Swiss organisation Helvetas.
The findings indicate that hunger reduction across South Asia has largely stalled, with Pakistan and Afghanistan experiencing worsening conditions since 2018. Pakistan’s economic difficulties and rising food inflation have weakened household purchasing power, leaving many families struggling to afford adequate nutrition. The country’s undernourishment indicator has worsened from a low level in 2018 to a medium level, while child wasting has approached the threshold for the high category.
South Asia’s overall Global Hunger Index score stands at 23.5, placing the region in the serious category. Although the score has improved from 37.5 in 2000, much of the progress occurred before 2018. Pakistan and Afghanistan have moved out of the alarming category over the past two decades, but persistent child malnutrition remains a major concern. Child stunting continues to decline in Pakistan, whereas Afghanistan has witnessed a slight increase since 2018. Child mortality has improved in both countries, falling from very high levels in 2000 to medium levels currently.
The report also highlighted the impact of extreme weather on regional food production. Heavy rainfall and flooding damaged crops in parts of Pakistan and Bangladesh, while insufficient rainfall and unusually high temperatures affected Afghanistan’s cereal-growing season in 2026. These climate pressures could prolong acute food insecurity, as highlighted by Dawn. Estimates from the Food and Agriculture Organisation suggest that 218 million people across South Asia, including Iran, suffered from undernourishment between 2023 and 2025, accounting for approximately one-third of the global total, as reported by Dawn. (ANI)

items.title: ＵＢＳ、本社の国外移転検討　資本規制強化に備え＝ＷＳＪ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１４日 ロイター] - スイスの金融大手ＵＢＳは、議会が資本規制を厳格化した場合に備え、本社の国外移転を含む対応策を準備している。米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）が１４日、事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。

選択肢には、米金融機関を買収して移転する案のほか、欧州の競合他社との合併、米銀への身売りなどが含まれるという。

スイスはＵＢＳによる２０２３年のクレディ・スイス救済を受け、「大きすぎてつぶせない」金融機関に対する資本規制の強化を検討している。

政府案はＵＢＳに対し、海外子会社を普通株式等Ｔｉｅｒ１（ＣＥＴ１）資本で１００％裏付けることなどを求めており、同社はＣＥＴ１資本を２００億ドル追加で保有する必要が生じる。現在は、主にＣＥＴ１資本で少なくとも６０％を裏付けることが求められている。

ＵＢＳは、１００％の要件は過剰で国際競争力を損なうとして、この案に反対している。

items.title: EXCLUSIVE-ＳＫハイニックス、米工場建設の条件に対中装置輸出拡大要求＝関係筋
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Karen Freifeld　Hyunjoo Jin

[１４日 ロイター] - 韓国のＳＫハイニックスは、米国での工場...
items.body:
EXCLUSIVE-ＳＫハイニックス、米工場建設の条件に対中装置輸出拡大要求＝関係筋
13:26 配信

2026年7月10日、米ナスダック市場に上場した際に撮影。REUTERS/Angelina Katsanis

Karen Freifeld　Hyunjoo Jin

[１４日 ロイター] - 韓国のＳＫハイニックスは、米国での工場建設の条件として、中国での増産に向けた米国製半導体製造装置の対中輸出許可を米政府に求めている。事情に詳しい関係者２人が１４日明らかにした。

トランプ米政権は、米国内の製造能力再建と雇用創出を目指し、ＳＫハイニックスやサムスン電子など外国の半導体メーカーに米国での工場建設を迫っている。

世界的なメモリー半導体不足で価格が上昇する中、ＳＫハイニックスの米子会社ソリダイムは、中国・大連にあるＳＫハイニックスの拠点の未使用区画に新たな装置を設置し、ＮＡＮＤ型フラッシュメモリーを生産したい考えだ。ＮＡＮＤ型フラッシュメモリーは、人工知能（ＡＩ）やクラウドコンピューティング向けのデータセンターに設置されるソリッドステートドライブ（ＳＳＤ）に使われる。

大連のＮＡＮＤ工場では、ラムリサーチ、アプライド・マテリアルズ、ＫＬＡなど米半導体製造装置大手の装置が使われている。

ソリダイムが大連向けの追加装置について米国の輸出許可を求めていることや、米国でのＮＡＮＤ新工場建設計画を中国工場と関連付けていることが報じられるのは初めて。

ＳＫハイニックスはロイターへの声明で「Ｍｏｄ Ｂへの装置設置は、米政府と緊密に協議し、その許可の下で進めている」と説明。「２０２３年に完成した大連のＭｏｄ Ｂについて、生産能力の拡大は求めていない」とした。

ソリダイムはコメントを控えた。

輸出管理を所管し、半導体製造施設への投資について交渉してきた米商務省は、コメント要請に応じなかった。

ロイターは９月、ソリダイムが米国でＮＡＮＤ型フラッシュメモリー工場の建設を検討していると報じた。 

関係者の１人によると、中国での増産はソリダイムが米国のＮＡＮＤ工場建設資金を確保する助けとなり、米国内での増産までのつなぎにもなる。

items.title: Vijay Mallya's flamboyant lifestyle delaying loan settlement: Karnataka HC
items.summary: The court made the observation while granting relief to Diageo Holdings Netherlands BV in a dispute over shares held by Mallya in UBL ...
items.body:
Home / India News / Vijay Mallya's flamboyant lifestyle delaying loan settlement: Karnataka HC

Vijay Mallya's flamboyant lifestyle delaying loan settlement: Karnataka HC The court made the observation while granting relief to Diageo Holdings Netherlands BV in a dispute over shares held by Mallya in UBL

Vijay Mallya (REUTERS/File Photo)

Vrinda Goel New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 4:36 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday observed that former Kingfisher Airlines promoter Vijay Mallya’s “flamboyant lifestyle” appeared to be hindering the closure of loan recovery proceedings pending against the now-defunct airline, Bar and Bench reported.
  A Division Bench made the observation while granting relief to Diageo Holdings Netherlands BV in a dispute over shares held by Mallya in United Breweries Limited (UBL), which had been pledged in connection with a loan.
  The Bench noted that even decades of work could be undone when the focus shifted from operational excellence and financial prudence to “personal vanity, outsized egos and hedonistic excess”. The court said that when disciplined grit was replaced by a cult of personality and hubris, the result could be bankruptcy and ruin.
 

  Recounting Mallya’s rise in the liquor business and the expansion of his empire, the Bench noted that he came to be known as the “King of Good Times”, with his flamboyant lifestyle becoming inseparable from the brand he built. His “debt-fuelled gamble” on Kingfisher Airlines, however, collapsed, eventually leading to his status as a fugitive economic offender, it added.
  “More than anything else, we are also of the view that it is Dr Vijay Mallya’s flamboyant lifestyle, excessive personal indulgence and his personal vanity are coming in the way of giving quietus to the claims of the Consortium of Banks against the loan of ₹6,203 crore advanced to the defunct Kingfisher Airlines Ltd,” the court observed.

Also Read

Jio eyes big share of India's digital economy: Akash Ambani ahead of IPO

Actor Imran Khan asked to leave India: What law says about OCI cardholders

EPFO extends PF filing deadline to Oct 31: What employees should check

Why was IDBI Bank sold at ₹81 a share? Understanding the valuation

  The court held that Diageo’s claim ranked higher than the banks’ entitlement to these shares. It also noted that the banks had already recovered assets worth ₹14,131.6 crore against the ₹6,203 crore loan extended to Kingfisher Airlines. The court held that the banks were not justified in staking a claim over the UBL shares as well. The Bench added that it was now up to the consortium of banks and the government to close the loan recovery proceedings.
  How did Vijay Mallya respond?   Responding to the court’s remarks, Mallya said in a post on X that he was being punished for living a “Kingsize” life with his own money.

  “Am I still a Chor or Cheat?” he said. “I lived life Kingsize with my own money and that was my biggest crime for which I am being punished."   Order passed by a Division Bench of the Hon’ble Karnataka High Court. I sincerely request you to read carefully. Am I still a Chor or Cheat ? I lived life Kingsize with my own money and that was my biggest crime for which I am being punished . There is a God above for all of us. Someday Justice will prevail.
— Vijay Mallya (@TheVijayMallya) October 14, 2026
  What is the case about?   The case before the court concerned UBL shares held by Mallya individually, as well as shares jointly held by him and his son, Sidhartha Mallya, in United Breweries.
  Diageo’s claim arose from a $135 million loan that Standard Chartered Bank (SCB) extended to Watson Ltd, an overseas company of Mallya, in July 2013. The loan was secured by a pledge of UBL shares, and Diageo guaranteed it. After Watson defaulted, Diageo paid the bank $140.97 million in January 2016 and claimed to have stepped into SCB’s shoes.

  A consortium of banks, however, had obtained certain interim orders in recovery proceedings against Kingfisher Airlines, freezing the shares. The banks argued that the UBL shares could be used to recover the ₹6,203 crore owed to them by Kingfisher Airlines and that Diageo’s pledge over the shares was ineffective.
  Mallya and UBL had guaranteed repayment of the loan under a Master Debt Recast Agreement dated December 21, 2010.
  Diageo approached the high court for relief after the Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) and the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal (DRAT) ruled against it. The high court held that the pledge created in favour of SCB in 2013 had priority over the bank consortium’s claim under the 2010 agreement.

  The court also noted that Sidhartha Mallya was not a party to the Master Debt Recast Agreement with the banks. It further held that Mallya’s personal guarantee did not, by itself, create a proprietary charge over the jointly held shares.
  Mallya left India in 2016 and lives in the UK. He was declared a fugitive economic offender in 2019, and India has long sought his extradition over alleged loan defaults and money laundering.

items.title: EU leaders kick off summit with wrangles over high energy prices and spending
items.author: Philip Blenkinsop, Kate Abnett
items.creator: Philip Blenkinsop, Kate Abnett
items.summary: The European Union began a packed summit on Thursday that quickly underscored wrangles over how to tame soaring energy prices, design a budget to keep the bloc competitive and curb surging exports from China that are blamed for job losses.
items.body:
The European Union began a packed summit on Thursday that quickly underscored wrangles over how to tame soaring energy prices, design a budget to keep the bloc competitive and curb surging exports from China that are blamed for job losses.
The leaders from the EU's 27 members met in Brussels on the back of securing an [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"agreement with Beijing"] to limit imports of hybrid cars from China, a first step towards cutting a goods trade deficit that hit €360 billion ($400 billion) in 2025.
The summit takes place at a time of heightened economic anxiety, with fuel price spikes since the Iran war putting cash-strapped governments on the back foot, companies struggling and Europe wanting to shore up its defences and [USN:L6N4610BB TEXT:"support Ukraine"].
The clock is also ticking on a series of elections in Europe over the coming months including in France in April, which could propel French [USN:L8N4601WM TEXT:"far-right leader Marine Le Pen"] to the presidency vowing to slash her country's contribution to the EU budget.
Slumping in the polls at home, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told reporters that positions were still far apart on the budget, which has pitted net contributors such as Germany against net beneficiaries. The latest proposal would safeguard subsidies for farmers and regions, which critics say sucks money away from more urgent areas to keep up with the US and China.
"We are, therefore, facing very, very difficult negotiations," Merz said.
MERZ SAYS FROZEN RUSSIAN ASSETS MUST STAY IN EUROPE Merz also gave a [USN:L6N4610ML TEXT:"pointed rebuff"] to a proposal by the United States, reported in the Financial Times, for European countries to unfreeze some Russian sovereign assets immobilised after the invasion of Ukraine . The idea would be to transfer them to a vehicle overseen by Washington in an attempt to revive peace talks, the FT reported, citing people briefed on the matter.
"These are assets that are frozen in Europe, and they should remain frozen in Europe. This is our affair, and we are the ones who decide on it," Merz said.
While France is also a net contributor to the EU budget, its officials warned that a blunt focus on spending cuts would be counterproductive, hobbling measures that were also intended to make the bloc more competitive.
"We can clearly see that cuts alone cannot resolve the equation," one official said.
Draft conclusions from the summit indicate leaders want the Commission to continue talks with Beijing, while also making full use of EU trade defence measures and adding new trade instruments to protect the bloc further.
"These imbalances are not limited to one sector. We don't have much time because every month that goes by, thousands of jobs are lost," said a senior EU diplomat.
Beijing has said that hyping up the issue of economic imbalances is an excuse to promote protectionism and exert pressure on and restrict China.
"We don't have enough measures to counter unfair practices, we have also not invested enough in our own competitiveness and innovation, the new EU budget will need to be equipped for that," Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten told reporters.
GERMANY'S U-TURN ON CHINA IMPORTS [USN:L6N45R0Q0 TEXT:"Franco-German proposals"] released last week are also likely to be the focus of discussions. The EU's two largest economies said there was an urgent need for measures to deal with imports of chemicals and PET — the plastic widely used in packaging — and called for measures to retaliate quickly against countries that harm the bloc.
The paper marks a sharp turn for Germany, which only two years ago was the most vocal critic of EU anti-subsidy tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles.
Several EU countries have also put high energy prices on the agenda.
One area of contention is the wish by countries including the Czech Republic and Italy [USN:L1N45L09G TEXT:"to weaken or suspend"] the EU Emissions Trading System, a regulation forcing power plants and industries to buy CO2 permits when they pollute.
The prime ministers of Finland, Sweden and Denmark hit back in a letter praising the system as a driver of energy security by helping Europe reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels. They warned "any weakening" would hinder investment in clean industries.
One of Friday's main topics will be the challenges facing Ukraine, with President [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"Volodymyr Zelenskiy"] due to attend at a time when Kyiv is at [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"loggerheads with the US"] over intelligence sharing while missiles and drones hammer Ukrainian cities.
Leaders are expected to discuss Ukraine's funding needs for 2027, with Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs comparing the cost to each citizen of the price of a beer.
"It is one beer less for one European a year. We can afford that. But Ukraine needs it now," he said.
($1 = €0.8991)

items.title: BP Can Solve Its Debt Problem Once and For All
items.author: Javier Blas
items.creator: Javier Blas
items.summary: Fortune favors the bold — and the frugal. BP Plc decided in early February to suspend its $3 billion-a-year share buyback program. The move wasn’t popular with every shareholder, but it was necessary to preserve cash to pay down debt instead. Days later, the US and Israel attacked Iran, sending energy prices sharply higher. The ensuing windfall, plus the buyback savings, have created an unmissable opportunity: The British oil major can solve its balance-sheet problems once and for all.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Manya Saini　Saeed Azhar　Tatiana Bautzer

[１４日 ロイター] - 米大手銀行は...
items.body:
アングル：米大手銀、ＡＩブームの波に乗る一方で警戒も　収益機会とリスクが併存
12:38 配信

写真は人工知能（ＡＩ）のイメージ。9月23日に撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Manya Saini　Saeed Azhar　Tatiana Bautzer

[１４日 ロイター] - 米大手銀行は人工知能（ＡＩ）ブームに乗りつつも荒波に巻き込まれるのを避けたい意向だ。ＡＩインフラ向け融資が巨額の収益機会をもたらすと期待される一方、投資収益への疑問や新たなセキュリティー上の脅威が浮上しているためだ。

米大手銀行の幹部からは今週、ＡＩエージェントが顧客に代わって行動するリスクや、ＡＩの急速な普及に必要な資本と計算能力への需要を巡る不透明感に関する発言が相次いだ。

ゴールドマン・サックスのデービッド・ソロモン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）はアナリストとの電話会議で、「ＡＩ投資サイクルで当社が重要な役割を担っていることを誇りに思う。一方、ＡＩのエコシステム全体が成熟するにつれ、資本と計算能力への需要がどう変化するかは誰にも分からない」と発言。「テクノロジーと市場が発展し続けるなかで、状況は次第に明らかになるだろう。この不確実性があるからこそ、どのような活動に融資するのか、リスクをどう管理するのかについて、警戒を怠らないことが重要だ」と語った。

シティグループのジェーン・フレーザーＣＥＯは、「ＡＩエコシステム全体で、投資の減速は見られない。単純に、計算能力が不足している」と述べ、金利上昇によってＡＩインフラへの投資が鈍化することはないとの見解を示した。

＜ＡＩ向け融資はビジネスチャンス＞

ＡＩインフラへの投資規模は前例のない水準に達している。大手テクノロジー企業は、生成ＡＩモデルの学習や稼働に必要な計算能力の基盤となるデータセンターの建設に、数十億ドル規模の資金を投じる方針を示している。米銀にとって、このインフラ整備は、数十年に一度ともいえる大規模な投資サイクルへの融資機会となる。

バンク・オブ・アメリカのブライアン・モイニハンＣＥＯは、ＡＩ関連の巨額設備投資が同行の投資適格債事業やレバレッジド・ファイナンス事業にとって重要だと述べた。

しかし融資機会が実際に実を結ぶには、いくつもの不確定要素に左右される。計算能力への需要が業界の野心的な拡張計画に追いつくのか、データセンター事業がどれほどの投資収益を生み出せるのか、地元で反対運動が起きる可能性はないのか、といった点だ。

ウェルズ・ファーゴのチャーリー・シャーフＣＥＯは決算発表後のアナリスト向け電話会議で、「ＡＩ投資サイクルは、それ自体が複雑なマクロ経済要因となっている」と述べた。そしてデータセンターなどの整備は大きな事業機会をもたらす一方、多額の借り入れを伴う資金調達や、一部の業界・サプライチェーンでの価格上昇圧力など、リスクも伴うと指摘した。その上で、「これまでのところ、経済の底堅さと、こうした投資がもたらすプラスの効果が、潜在的なマイナス面を上回っている」と述べた。

ただ、金利が高止まりしたり、さらに上昇したりすれば、データセンター事業の資金調達コストが膨らみ、投資収益が圧迫される可能性がある。また、借り手にとって債務返済の負担も重くなる。

モルガン・スタンレーのシャロン・イェシャヤ最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）はロイターとのインタビューで、同行は引き受けるリスクの種類を「非常に慎重に見極めている」と述べた。「懸念されるのは、同業他社などが融資基準を緩め、それが問題を引き起こすことだ。当社は、そうした取引に関与しないよう細心の注意を払っている」という。一方、同社のテッド・ピックＣＥＯはアナリストとの電話会議で、ＡＩ関連融資への関与は同社にとって「極めて重要だ」と述べた。

投資家も、ＡＩブームがもたらす経済的な恩恵と、融資が損失につながるリスクを見極めている。

複数の銀行株を保有するガベリ・ファンズのポートフォリオマネジャー、マクレー・サイクス氏は、「テクノロジー関連支出が経済全体の成長を後押ししている限り、銀行にとって重要なプラス材料だ。ただ、投機的なデータセンター建設のような特定の事業に信用リスクが直接結び付いている場合、将来問題につながる可能性がある」と述べた。

一方で、銀行は懸念されているよりもＡＩ関連リスクをしっかりと管理しているとの見方もある。各行が金融危機後にリスク管理の慣行を厳格化してきたためだ。

ヘネシー・ファンズのポートフォリオマネジャー、デーブ・エリソン氏は、銀行は金融危機の教訓を忘れておらず、投資家が懸念する以上に慎重に行動していると述べた。銀行はＡＩ関連融資を支えているものの、リスクを投資家に分散するアレンジャーの役割を果たしている場合が多いという。

＜新たなＡＩリスクの封じ込め＞

銀行はインフラ整備向け融資に加え、コスト削減や生産性向上を目指して自社業務にＡＩを導入している。しかし、導入による財務上の効果を測るのは、依然として難しい。

ＪＰモルガン・チェースのジェレミー・バーナムＣＦＯは、「このテーマがどれほど重要で、大きな変化をもたらすものであっても、当行ほどの規模の金融機関で目に見える形で成果を出すには長い時間がかかる」と述べ、四半期決算にまだ効果が表れていないのは想定内だとの見方を示した。

一方、シティグループのフレーザーＣＥＯは、ＡＩ活用による明確な効果がすでに表れていると説明した。例えば、製品開発のコストを抑えながら、開発期間を最大４０％短縮できているほか、コーディング支援ツールの活用によって開発作業が容易になり、技術関連の外部委託先への支出を３０％削減できたという。

items.title: ＴＡＰポルトガル航空、ルフトハンザが最大49.9％株式を取得へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Sergio Goncalves　Joanna Plucinska

[リスボン １４日 ロイター] - ポルトガル政府...
items.body:
ＴＡＰポルトガル航空、ルフトハンザが最大49.9％株式を取得へ
12:23 配信

写真は２０２１年３月、アイルランドのダブリン空港から離陸するＴＡＰポルトガル航空機。REUTERS/Clodagh Kilcoyne

Sergio Goncalves　Joanna Plucinska

[リスボン １４日 ロイター] - ポルトガル政府は１４日、国有企業のＴＡＰポルトガル航空の株式の最大４９．９％をドイツのルフトハンザ航空に売却すると発表した。取得額は１２億ユーロ（約１３億ドル）となる見込みで、ルフトハンザはＴＡＰの戦略的な提携相手となる。

ＴＡＰを巡っては、欧州航空大手のエールフランスＫＬＭも株式取得を目指して競っていた。ポルトガルのルイス・モンテネグロ首相は記者会見で、ルフトハンザの落札額がエールフランスＫＬＭの提示額を１６％上回っていたと明らかにした。

イラン戦争でジェット燃料価格が高騰しているのを受け、アナリストや業界幹部らは、規模が大きくて資本力のある航空グループが経営基盤の弱い航空会社との提携を加速する可能性が高いと指摘している。

オーストリア航空、イタリアのＩＴＡエアウェイズ（旧アリタリア航空）、スイス航空などを傘下に持つルフトハンザはＴＡＰの提携相手になることで、欧州南西部や世界の他地域へのアクセスを拡大できる。航空アナリストのジョン・ストリックランド氏はロイターに対して「これによってルフトハンザは影響力が及んでいない地域で、新たなハブ（拠点）空港を得ることになる」と指摘。一方で「ルフトハンザは依然として赤字を計上しており、まずは自社の経営を立て直さなければならない」と言及した。

ＴＡＰはリスボン空港にブラジル、アフリカのポルトガル語圏諸国、米国を結ぶ路線の発着枠を抱えている。これらの路線はポルトガルへの観光や投資を呼び込んでいる。

発表に先立ってリスボンで開催された世界航空フェスティバルで講演したＴＡＰのルイス・ロドリゲス最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、大規模なグループに加わることで「より大きな経営資源を、より有利な条件で活用できる」と語った。

ポルトガル政府はリスボン空港だけではなく、ポルト、ファロ、アゾレス諸島、マデイラ島を含めた国内空港の運航網拡大を求めている。インフラ相のミゲル・ピント・ルス氏は、ルフトハンザが３５年までにＴＡＰの航空機を１１７機に増強し、リスボンの新空港の運用開始が見込まれる２０３５年以降は１３０機に増やすことを約束したと表明した。

ＴＡＰは今年６月時点で１０１機を運用し、世界の９３地点を結んでいる。うち欧州が５２地点、中南米が１６地点、アフリカが１４地点、北米が１１地点。２６年上半期の旅客数は約８２０万人と過去最高になり、前年同期比で４．２％伸びた。２６年上半期の売上高に当たる営業収益は４．３％増えた。

items.title: エヌビディア、英国のＡＩ安全性研究に2.5億ドル相当の計算資源提供
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ロンドン １４日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手エヌビディアは、人工知能（ＡＩ）の安全性に関する研究を支援するため、今...
items.body:
エヌビディア、英国のＡＩ安全性研究に2.5億ドル相当の計算資源提供
12:18 配信

2026年6月11日撮影のイラスト。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[ロンドン １４日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手エヌビディアは、人工知能（ＡＩ）の安全性に関する研究を支援するため、今後５年間で総額２億５０００万ドル相当の計算資源を英国に提供すると表明した。ＡＩのガバナンスと安全性の分野で世界的な拠点となることを目指す英国の取り組みを後押しする。

英国には主要なＡＩ開発企業の本社は存在しないものの、同国はＡＩシステムがもたらすリスクの評価や管理において主導的な役割を果たそうとしている。その一環として、ＡＩ技術を評価するために設立された政府支援機関であるＡＩセキュリティー研究所を活用している。

エヌビディアの創業者であるジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１４日、英国に対し年間５０００万ドル相当の高速計算資源を提供すると述べた。これらの資源はエージェント型ＡＩの安全性試験に充てられ、ますます高性能化するＡＩに対する安全対策の強化を英国の研究者が進める上で役立つという。

フアン氏は「ＡＩの能力向上と安全性の向上は、同時に進めなければならない」と強調。「これによって英国は、研究分野でのリーダーシップを現実社会の解決策へと転換し、科学的進歩をすべての人々に恩恵をもたらす未来へと結び付けることができる」と語った。

アンソロピックやオープンＡＩなどの開発企業がＡＩエージェントによる暴走や望ましくない行動の事例を公表したことを受け、ＡＩの安全性に対する監視は強まっている。一部の業界関係者は、この技術が人類の存続そのものを脅かす可能性があると警告している。

英国のカニシュカ・ナラヤンＡＩ担当相は、エヌビディアからの提供によって、将来のＡＩが「安全で信頼性が高く、人々の最善の利益にかなうもの」であることを確実にする助けになると述べた。

items.title: Gold climbs over 1% on softer dollar, yields ahead of US inflation data
items.author: Sherin Sans
items.creator: Sherin Sans
items.summary: Gold prices climbed more than 1% on Thursday as the dollar and US Treasury yields remained under pressure, while investors looked to fresh US inflation data for clues on whether the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again this month.
items.body:
Gold prices climbed more than 1% on Thursday as the dollar and US Treasury yields remained under pressure, while investors looked to fresh US inflation data for clues on whether the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again this month.
Spot gold was up 1.3% to $4,156.58 per ounce by 1124 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery rose 1.7% to $4,178.50 per ounce.
The dollar (.DXY) slipped 0.5%, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for holders of other currencies, while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield also fell to a three-week low.
"Falling real yields and resilient investment demand help gold recover from its post-CPI selloff, but the technical outlook remains fragile," said Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank.
[USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"US consumer prices"] accelerated in September on a surge in gasoline costs, with price pressures spreading beyond energy and raising concerns among economists that underlying inflation could be getting sticky.
Market participants are now awaiting Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales data due at 1230 GMT for further clues on inflation trends and the Federal Reserve's policy path.
"If the PPI comes in as expected, which is 5.4% year on year, then that pattern will be continued. So you would expect bond yields to rise again. We're just going to have to watch it very carefully," said Rhona O'Connell, head of market analysis at Stone X.
Traders are pricing in about a 29% chance of a rate hike later this month, compared with 22% before the data, according to CME's FedWatch Tool .
Gold is traditionally seen as a hedge against inflation, but higher interest rates make the non-yielding asset less attractive.
San Francisco Fed President [USN:L6N4601E8 TEXT:"Mary Daly"] said further rate increases would probably be needed, but signalled no need to act at the October meeting; Vice Chair for Supervision [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"Michelle Bowman"] said there was time to wait.
Among other metals, spot silver gained 1.9% to $56.69 per ounce, platinum rose 0.7% to $1,617.50 per ounce and palladium climbed 3.5% to $1,132 per ounce.

items.title: India's exports to US rise 11%, imports jump 26% amid ongoing trade talks
items.summary: India's merchandise exports to the United States rose 11.1 per cent to USD 50.81 billion during April–September 2026, despite tariff-related disruptions, while imports from the US increased by 26 per ...
items.body:
India's exports to US rise 11%, imports jump 26% amid ongoing trade talks India's merchandise exports to the United States rose 11.1 per cent to USD 50.81 billion during April–September 2026, despite tariff-related disruptions, while imports from the US increased by 26 per cent, according to data presented by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Thursday.
ANI | Updated: 15-10-2026 15:41 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 15:41 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India's merchandise exports to the United States rose 11.1 per cent to USD 50.81 billion during April–September 2026, despite tariff-related disruptions, while imports from the US increased by 26 per cent, according to data presented by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Thursday. Exports to the US increased from USD 45.73 billion in the corresponding period last year, while imports rose to USD 32.33 billion from USD 25.66 billion.
The figures show that bilateral trade continued to expand despite tariff uncertainties, although India's merchandise trade surplus with the US narrowed to USD 18.48 billion from USD 20.07 billion a year earlier. The US remained India's largest merchandise export destination during the first half of the current financial year.
Meanwhile, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said negotiations for the proposed India-US trade agreement were progressing in the right direction, with both countries working towards concluding the deal at the earliest. "The negotiations are in the right direction. Probably, we are in a very good zone. We anticipate closing the deal and signing it at the earliest possible time," Agrawal said during a press briefing.
He explained that the agreement would depend on the finalisation of the broader tariff framework in the United States, where a parallel process is underway under Section 301. "The deal has to be signed when the overall tariff structure is getting formalised. There is parallel work being done in the US also to get back the tariff structure based on some of the outcomes of the 301," he said.
Agrawal further emphasised that India was seeking preferential access to the American market to ensure its exporters could compete effectively with other countries. "When you do a trade deal, it gives you not only market access in each other's markets; it gives you preferential market access in a particular market," he said.
He added that India's preferential market access relative to its competitors would form part of the new tariff framework. The ongoing negotiations are significant as both countries seek to strengthen bilateral trade ties while addressing tariff-related challenges affecting market access. (ANI)

items.title: イラン経済崩壊との米国の主張は幻想＝中銀総裁
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ドバイ １４日 ロイター] - イラン中央銀行のヘンマティ総裁は１４日、イラン経済が崩壊しているとする米国の主張は幻...
items.body:
イラン経済崩壊との米国の主張は幻想＝中銀総裁
12:06 配信

１３日、イランの首都テヘランのグランドバザールに集まる人々。マージド・アスガリプール/WANA（西アジア通信社）提供。REUTERS

[ドバイ １４日 ロイター] - イラン中央銀行のヘンマティ総裁は１４日、イラン経済が崩壊しているとする米国の主張は幻想だと述べた。バンコクで開催された国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）年次総会で発言した。

ヘンマティ氏は、中銀が医薬品や生活必需品のための外貨を確保しつつ、インフレの抑制、インフレ期待の安定化、金融の安定性、銀行・決済サービスの維持を優先していると語った。イラン統計庁によると、９月のインフレ率は年率７３．６％に達した。

中銀は９月下旬、通貨リアルを支えるために国営銀行を通じて最大２０億ドルを売却するプログラムを開始している。

米政府はイランの石油輸出を絶って国庫を枯渇させることを目的に、７月に同国の港湾封鎖を再開。８月２４日にはイランと外国の金融・商業的つながりを断ち切ることを狙った「オペレーション・エコノミック・アウトキャスト（経済的追放作戦）」を開始した。

エネルギー情報プラットフォームのボルテクサによると、イランの海上原油輸出量は、９月初め時点で１４日間平均が日量２３万バレルだったのが、同月第２週にはゼロになり、１０月５日現在もゼロのままだ。

米国は９月、イランの航空会社を標的に加えて同国をさらに孤立させた。

米国の圧力と並行してリアル相場は急落しており、イランの為替データサイト、ボンバストによると７月以降、米ドルに対して約３５％下落した。

items.body:
午前の日経平均は大幅に続落、4％超安　ＡＩ期待に揺り戻し
12:05 配信

都内の株価ボード前で6月撮影。REUTERS/Manami Yamada

Noriyuki Hirata

[東京 １５日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は大幅に続落し、前営業日比４．８１％（３２５５円２３銭）安の６万４４８９円０６銭となった。注目された米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）の結果を受けた下押しは限定的との見方がある一方、人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービス米大手の社債価格や株価が急落し、ＡＩ成長期待の揺り戻しが警戒された。午後には台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が決算を発表する予定となっており、相場反応に関心が寄せられる。

・日経平均は安く寄り付いた後も下げを拡大し、安値で午前の取引を終えた。

・日銀の小枝淳子審議委員が「物価上昇リスクが相応にあることを踏まえれば利上げに過度に慎重になることはない」などと発言。相場反応は限定的か。

・ＴＯＰＩＸは２．５２％安の３９９３．５０ポイントで午前の取引を終了。

・東証プライム市場の売買代金は４兆５３５０億４０００万円。

・東証３３業種で上昇は、医薬品、パルプ・紙、小売など９業種、下落は非鉄金属、電気機器、ガラス・土石など２４業種。

・東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが５０９銘柄（３２％）、値下がりは１０１０銘柄（６５％）、変わらずは３２銘柄（２％）。

＜大和証券　チーフストラテジスト　坪井裕豪氏＞

items.title: The bull market turns four. Is age really just a number?: Stan Wong
items.summary: At four years old, the current bull market remains about a year and a half younger than the historical average. Of course, this does not mean another 18 months of gains are assured. Rather, it ...
items.body:
“I’m still standing (yeah, yeah, yeah).”
Elton John’s famous lyric seems particularly fitting as the S&P 500 bull market celebrates its fourth birthday this week.

On Oct. 12, 2022, the S&P 500 closed at 3,577, roughly 25 per cent below its previous peak. Inflation was running at multidecade highs, the Federal Reserve was aggressively raising interest rates, recession forecasts were widespread and investor sentiment was deeply pessimistic.
Yet that October low marked the beginning of a new bull market, generally defined as a sustained rise of at least 20 per cent from a previous market low. Since then, the S&P 500 has climbed more than 118 per cent, excluding dividends, overcoming considerable economic uncertainty and several significant corrections.
But is this bull market beginning to show its age, or could there still be room to run?
Four years old, but not necessarily old Investors often assume that the longer a bull market lasts, the closer it must be to ending. However, market cycles do not follow a predetermined timetable.
My analysis of Bloomberg data examined 11 completed S&P 500 bull markets dating back to 1949. The average lasted about 5.5 years, although durations varied considerably. The shortest continued for just 21 months, from 2020 to 2022, while the longest persisted for more than 12 years, from 1987 to 2000.
At four years old, the current bull market remains about a year and a half younger than the historical average. Of course, this does not mean another 18 months of gains are assured. Rather, it illustrates why market age alone is a poor indicator of when a bull market might end.
While bull market longevity provides useful historical context, an even more interesting question is how stocks have performed after reaching their fourth anniversary.
What happens in year five? Of the 11 completed bull markets since 1949, six lasted long enough to complete their fifth year.
Further analysis of Bloomberg data showed that all six generated positive S&P 500 price returns during their fifth year, averaging 17.4 per cent.
Returns ranged from 4.5 per cent during the bull market that began in 1987 to an impressive 30.4 per cent during the fifth year of the advance that started in 1982.
More recently, the bull market that emerged from the global financial crisis gained another 23.3 per cent during its fifth year, eventually continuing until February 2020.
While encouraging, these findings reflect a relatively small sample of bull markets that survived five full years. They provide historical perspective rather than a reliable forecast of future returns. The impressive fifth-year gain following the 1982 market bottom, for example, was followed just two months later by the October 1987 stock market crash.
History offers perspective, not a timetable.
Corrections are part of the journey Even long-running bull markets rarely advance in a straight line.
Consider 2025, when the S&P 500 declined nearly 19 per cent on a closing basis between February and April, approaching the conventional 20 per cent threshold that defines a bear market.
Yet the broader bull market survived, subsequently recovering and advancing to new highs. Investors who interpreted that correction as the beginning of a prolonged downturn risked missing the recovery.
It serves as an important reminder that market volatility and the end of a bull market are not necessarily the same thing.
Fundamentals matter more than birthdays Rather than focusing on market age, investors should pay closer attention to corporate earnings, valuations and economic conditions.
Artificial intelligence investment continues to support capital spending across industries, but elevated valuations and high expectations leave less room for disappointment. Broader market participation is also important, as a rally supported by more sectors and companies generally provides a healthier foundation than one dependent on a handful of market leaders.
Meanwhile, rising oil prices could reignite inflationary pressures, complicating monetary policy and keeping bond yields elevated. Ultimately, corporate profitability, valuations, interest rates and investor expectations will determine whether the bull market continues, not how many birthdays it has celebrated.
Investing beyond the birthday Selling simply because a bull market has lasted longer than expected can be costly. So can assuming recent gains will continue indefinitely.
Four years later, this bull market is still standing. For investors, the priority remains maintaining appropriate diversification, evaluating fundamentals and valuations, and aligning investment decisions with objectives, time horizons and risk tolerance within the context of each client’s broader total wealth plan.

items.author: ロイター

Leika Kihara

items.body:
ＩＭＦ、アジアの成長鈍化警告　利回り上昇波及リスク
11:56 配信

写真は１０月、国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会に出席する男性。タイのバンコクにあるクイーン・シリキット国立コンベンションセンターで撮影。REUTERS/Patipat Janthong

Leika Kihara

[バンコク １５日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１５日、アジアの経済成長が２０２７年に減速するとの見通しを示した。イラン戦争に伴うエネルギーショックや人工知能（ＡＩ）ブームの調整の可能性、世界的な債券利回り上昇の波及によるリスクが高まっていると警告した。

アジア太平洋地域の経済見通しに関する報告書で、米金融政策の先行きを巡る不確実性により、アジアの金融市場で不安定な動きが続く可能性も指摘した。

「今年のエネルギーショック以降、為替相場と資本フローの変動が大きくなっている」とし、複数の新興国で通貨の下落圧力が生じていると指摘。

域内への投資資金流入は総じて底堅さを維持しているものの、同時に韓国のハイテク株などからの資金の流出も生じているとした。

また「米金融政策のスタンスは年内さらに引き締められる見通しだ。主要先進国の大半で金融引き締めと財政面の圧力が重なり、アジア太平洋地域全体の利回りに上昇圧力をかけ続ける可能性が高い」とした。

アジア経済の成長率は２６年が４．８％、２７年は４．４％との見通しを示した。４月時点の予測から上方修正したが、２５年の５．０％からは減速する見通しだ。

上方修正は主に、ＡＩブームによるアジア先進国の成長押し上げを反映した。アジア先進国の成長率は２５年の２．５％から、２６年には３．２％に加速すると予想した。

アジア新興国は引き続き域内の主な成長けん引役だが、エネルギー価格上昇の打撃により、成長率は２５年の５．６％から２６年には５．１％に鈍化する見通しとした。

ＩＭＦは、中東紛争の膠着状態が長引けば、コモディティー（商品）価格が高止まりし、石油備蓄が枯渇する可能性があるとして、「見通しを巡るリスクは引き続き下振れ方向に傾いている」との見方を示した。

また、ＡＩ需要の調整は世界の成長を下押しする可能性があり、ＡＩ関連の生産網との関わりが深いアジアでは、その影響が特に顕著になる恐れがあるとした。

世界的に債券利回りが上昇する中、米英日、ユーロ圏など主要な国債発行国・地域の市場で生じたストレスがアジアの債券市場に波及し、利回りを押し上げ、既に高まっている財政の脆弱性を一段と悪化させる恐れがあるとも指摘した。

「域内の多くの国・地域で公的債務と資金調達需要が高水準にある中、金融環境が急激に引き締まれば、債務返済コストが増加し、財政が一段と圧迫される可能性がある」とした。

アジアの中央銀行は引き続き物価安定を重視し、インフレ圧力がより持続的になった場合には「速やかに対応」すべきだと述べた。

財政政策については、対象を絞った一時的な措置にすべきとし、より大きなコストを伴う恐れのある一律の燃料補助金や価格統制を回避するよう促した。

＜物価安定への焦点＞

ＩＭＦアジア太平洋地域局長のクリシュナ・スリニバーサン氏は記者会見で、アジアでは長期的なインフレ期待が概ね安定しているものの、中銀は引き続き物価の安定に注力すべきだと述べた。

「中銀は、インフレ期待が十分に安定していない場合、政策枠組みの信頼性が低い場合、あるいはインフレがより持続的な場合には、明確なメッセージを発信し、金融引き締めに備えるべきだ。これを支えるためには、中銀の独立性が維持されなければならない」とした。

公的債務がパンデミック（新型コロナウイルス大流行）前の水準を上回ったままであるため、追加の財政支出の余地はますます狭まっていると指摘。財政政策は対象を絞った一時的なものであるべきだと述べ、域内各国に対し、より大きなコストを伴う恐れのある一律の燃料補助金や価格統制を避けるよう促した。

items.title: Firmus CEO's Aussie scapegoating has iota of truth
items.author: Antony Currie
items.creator: Antony Currie
items.summary: Oliver Curtis blamed his neocloud's failed $5 bln IPO on local buyers' dim views of risk-taking. Investors Down Under can be cautious. But the deal was over-hyped and valuation punchy, not to mention Firmus and its banks all failed to play to the market Curtis is blaming.
items.body:
Oliver Curtis has taken the blame game over Firmus Technologies' [USN:L6N45V00W TEXT:"IPO flop"] to a new level. Rather than acknowledging fault, or singling out the investment bankers or the punchy $30 billion valuation they sought, the co-CEO of the neocloud company pointed the finger squarely at his native country Australia for having "dim views of people taking a risk".
The self-styled "homegrown hero" is not alone. Down Under billionaire and Firmus shareholder James Packer lamented that the country "tends to tear down aggressive entrepreneurs and America builds them up". While these sound like typical throwing-toys-out-of-the-pram moments, both have a point, albeit a small one: The breadth of Australia's $2 trillion economy is a concern. Industries like car manufacturing and steelmaking have disappeared or shrunk. The country fell 10 places in the decade to 2024 to rank 74th on Harvard's Economic Complexity Index; of the OECD countries, only Chile has a lower score. Mining and banking account for around 60% of the domestic stock market capitalisation.
Yet that ignores the growing financial and existential fears about AI that have now spread to Firmus' US rival CoreWeave (CRWV.O) : on Wednesday its shares slumped 15% and its bonds due in 2032 traded below 80 cents on the dollar. Moreover, Firmus had heaps of red flags too, the biggest being backer Coatue Management cutting its IPO commitment by 90% to $100 million last week, the AFR reported.
Those factors would have understandably scared off the country's pension, or superannuation, funds that manage A$4.8 trillion ($3.3 trillion) of assets. While they have a reputation for being risk-averse, they have readily backed scrappy mining startups and fintech firms and some have ploughed money into unlisted data centre outfits like AirTrunk and CDC Data Centres. They have also been crying out for decent-sized IPOs. Firmus would have been the biggest ASX listing this millennium by almost 40%.
It's not as if Curtis, who a decade ago was jailed for insider trading, or his bankers - Bank of America, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley and Morgans Financial - were blissfully unaware of these conflicting dynamics. Yet they still tried to garner an IPO valuation triple Firmus' worth in an August funding round for a company with a minuscule track record, little revenue and a convicted criminal in the C-suite. If Curtis wants to revisit an IPO any time soon - perhaps on the Nasdaq - he'd better start dining on some humble pie.
Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn .
Firmus Technologies co-founder and co-CEO Oliver Curtis said that the failure of the neocloud company's IPO was "a missed opportunity for Australia, to be brutally honest". He made the comments on October 11 to Liam Mendes, a reporter from The Australian newspaper who tracked him down on the way to a meeting in Singapore.
Curtis also said: "It's about Australia understanding ultimately we should be a homegrown hero, manufacture amazing technology with an amazing pipeline of opportunity...it is disappointing that Australia decided that there was a mantra of disbelief...Australia will, generally, take dim views on people taking a risk."
Australian billionaire and Firmus investor James Packer echoed Curtis' comments on October 13, telling The Australian that "Australia tends to tear down aggressive entrepreneurs and America builds them up."

items.title: Comedian Russell Brand was a ruthless sexual predator, UK prosecutors say
items.author: CNA Lifestyle
items.summary: British comedian Russell Brand faces 7 charges involving rape, sexual assault and indecent assault against 6 women. He denies all allegations concerning incidents between 1999 and 2009.
items.body:

Comedian Russell Brand was a ruthless sexual predator, UK prosecutors say

British comedian Russell Brand faces 7 charges involving rape, sexual assault and indecent assault against 6 women. He denies all allegations concerning incidents between 1999 and 2009.

British actor and comedian Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court where he stands trial on charges of rape and sexual assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009, which he denies, in London, Britain, October 14, 2026. REUTERS/Jack Taylor

15 Oct 2026 10:08AM

FAST

Actor and comedian Russell Brand, once one of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters, was a ruthless predator who raped or abused six women to satisfy his voracious sexual appetite, prosecutors said on Wednesday (Oct 14).
Brand, 51, the former husband of US singer Katy Perry, is on trial facing three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault relating to six women from 1999 to 2009.
He denies all the accusations and will set out his defence in court at a later date.
"Today I feel blessed," he said as he arrived at London's Southwark Crown Court. "I feel of course concerned but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody involved."
DESIRE WAS INDISCRIMINATE, PROSECUTOR TELLS COURT

Russell Brand speaks to the media as he arrives at Southwark Crown Court in London, Wednesday Oct. 14, 2026. (Ben Whitley/PA via AP)

Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones said some of the six women had protested, while others had no opportunity to react to his advances. It had made no difference to Brand, she said.
"His desire, his strong desire, for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious," she said.
Although he could be funny and charming when he wanted something, he also had a childlike expectation his every desire should be met, she added.
"He was ruthless, he was calculating, he was manipulative and, the prosecution say, he was a sexual predator," Karmy-Jones said.
The alleged offences took place over a decade as Brand progressed from gigs as a stand-up comedian to a TV presenter, actor and Hollywood movie star.
FIRST ALLEGED OFFENCE IN 1999

British actor and comedian Russell Brand appears at Southwark Crown Court where he stands trial on charges of rape and sexual assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009, which he denies, in London, Britain, October 14, 2026, in this courtroom sketch. REUTERS/Julia Quenzler

The first is alleged to have occurred in 1999 when he was performing in a show on the fringe of the Labour Party Conference in Bournemouth.
The first complainant, who had watched the show and had assumed Brand was gay, said he had raped her in her hotel room where she had invited him to talk.
Mark Pinheiro, one of his co-performers at the show who Brand went on to live with for about a year, said Brand bragged that he had wanted to bed 5,000 women in his lifetime.
Giving evidence, Pinheiro said on their last morning in Bournemouth, Brand had returned to where they were staying looking flustered and told them they had to immediately leave.
Pinheiro said that, a couple of months later, Brand admitted he had met a woman the night before and things "may have gone a little bit too far".
Brand's lawyer Ian Winter suggested to Pinheiro that he did not mention that when he first contacted police and no such conversation took place, which Pinheiro rejected.
BRAND SAYS HE NEVER ENGAGED IN NON-CONSENSUAL ACTIVITY

Russell Brand speaks to the media as he arrives at Southwark Crown Court in London, Wednesday Oct. 14, 2026. (Ben Whitley/PA via AP)

The second charge relates to 2001, when he is accused of trying to drag a woman into a toilet cubicle at MTV Europe where she worked. Three years later, a woman said he had dragged her into a toilet cubicle in a bar before orally raping her.
Around the same time in 2004 or 2005, a woman working at a media company said he indecently assaulted her.
The fifth complainant, a fan, had consensual sex at his home in 2009 but then he anally raped her, the prosecutor said. The sixth, who worked for Channel 4, alleges Brand had demanded a massage and then pressed his face into her groin, also in 2009.
When interviewed by police, Brand declined to answer questions but provided written statements in which he said he did not remember the incidents and had never engaged in non-consensual activity, Karmy-Jones said.
WOMEN CAME FORWARD AFTER TV PROGRAMME The women involved did not know each other and did not contact the police until after a TV programme and a press report in 2023 in which anonymous allegations were made by other women, the prosecutor said.
Brand sat in the dock wearing a dark suit and thin, white scarf, staring forward intently. His trial, expected to last about six weeks, has attracted huge media attention.
The comedian, known for his flamboyant style and appearance, became famous in Britain before starring in a number of films including "Get Him to the Greek" in 2010, the same year he married Perry. They divorced in 2012.
More recently Brand has appeared in online broadcasts discussing US politics, religion and free speech.
 

Source: Reuters/mm

items.title: Dollar eases from 18-month high as Treasury yields fall; Fed hike bets ease
items.author: Sophie Kiderlin
items.creator: Sophie Kiderlin
items.summary: The dollar slipped from an 18-month peak on Thursday as a sharp drop in Treasury yields weighed on the greenback, while cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials tempered October hike expectations despite hot inflation data.
items.body:
The dollar slipped from an 18-month peak on Thursday as a sharp drop in Treasury yields weighed on the greenback, while cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials tempered October hike expectations despite hot inflation data.
The dollar index , which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, was last down 0.2% on the day at 102.03, having hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after US inflation figures came in stronger than expected.
That helped the euro bounce 0.5% from an 18-month trough to $1.1216, putting it on track for its biggest daily gain in nearly two months. Sterling strengthened 0.5% to $1.3253, remaining broadly steady after data showed that [USN:L8N4610AT TEXT:"Britain's economy unexpectedly grew"] 0.1% in August.
Markets turned [USN:L6N46100A TEXT:"cautious"] and trading became somewhat choppy as Wednesday's [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"hot US CPI reading"] initially bolstered bets on higher-for-longer Fed rates, and worries about AI companies' heavy debt burdens were revived, driving safe-haven flows into Treasuries.
The rally in US government bonds pushed the benchmark 10-year yield to 5.085% while the 30-year yield fell to 5.428%, both at around three-week lows.
As well as the moves in bond yields and jittery equities, with tech stocks especially taking a hit, Kit Juckes, chief FX strategist at Societe Generale, also noted that shifts in positioning played a role in the dollar's moves.
"The overall picture is I think one of a little bit of a tug of war between people who would like to look for a correction in the dollar. Because positioning's too big, we've come a long way, there's not really much new news, we've got a lot of rate hikes priced in and so on. And then the economic data, which can flip it," he said.
"I suspect it'll be choppy and uncomfortable until we've got past the retail sales and PPI numbers."
Both data points are due later in the day, with producer prices expected to show a jump in business costs last month.
Market pricing for an October Fed rate hike [USN:L6N4600VL TEXT:"rose sharply"] to 50% on the back of the CPI data, before a chorus of Fed officials – including Vice Chair for Supervision [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"Michelle Bowman"] and San Francisco Fed President [USN:L6N4601E8 TEXT:"Mary Daly"] – said the central bank could wait for a clearer picture ahead of the October 27 and 28 meeting, tempering those bets.
"Despite the whole CPI number coming slightly stronger than expected, I think markets have sort of taken the view that maybe it was not hot enough to force the Fed's hand for October," said Khoon Goh, the head of Asia research at ANZ.
"(The) October (meeting) is also just a few days before the midterm elections as well," he added. "And that's possibly why the market doesn't want to be more aggressive in pricing in for October."
Investors will also watch remarks from Fed officials including Chair Kevin Warsh at IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday for clues on the US central bank's next move.
The Australian dollar fetched $0.6919 , down 0.7%, after [USN:L1N46100L TEXT:"local employment"] unexpectedly slid in September, while the Japanese yen strengthened to 157.80 per dollar.

items.title: Oil prices slips as US weighs easing sanctions on 'shadow fleet'
items.author: Ahmad Ghaddar
items.creator: Ahmad Ghaddar
items.summary: Brent crude prices fell over 1% on Thursday as potential US steps to ease restrictions on Russia's "shadow fleet" tankers soothed price concerns, but attacks on ships in the Middle East and Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure limited the decline.
items.body:
Brent crude prices fell over 1% on Thursday as potential US steps to ease restrictions on Russia's "shadow fleet" tankers soothed price concerns, but attacks on ships in the Middle East and Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure limited the decline.
The international benchmark lost $1.15, or 1.1%, to $104.91 a barrel by 1157 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up marginally by 31 cents, or 0.3%, to $95.40, amid expectations for a large draw in weekly inventories.
Oil prices fell after a US official said on Wednesday that the US administration was considering [USN:L1N46017R TEXT:"easing sanctions"] on some of Russia's unregulated tankers, a move that could help lower freight rates and increase flexibility in diesel shipments, PVM Oil analyst John Evans said.
The discussions are happening days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, to ease a surge in prices globally. The new talks centre on Washington potentially allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said.
Prices, however, were still finding support from an escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis and renewed attacks on ships in the region.
A [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"container ship and a dry bulk carrier both sank"] near the strait after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday.
Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.
"The ongoing conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is keeping a geopolitical premium in oil markets, but energy infrastructure has not been attacked in the last several days," MUFG analysts said in a note.
Meanwhile, [USN:L6N4610BB TEXT:"Ukraine resumed its attacks"] on Russian refineries with a strike on a plant in the Ryazan region, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy voiced anger at a "dangerous" withdrawal of US intelligence.
Spain will [USN:L6N4610OA TEXT:"release"] 4.4 million barrels from strategic reserves in October, an Energy Ministry official said on Thursday, as the International Energy Agency began a meeting expected to clarify details of a 100 million-barrel oil stock release, including diesel, with the timing and scale of the move in focus.
In the US, crude oil and distillate inventories fell, while gasoline stocks rose last week, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.
Crude stocks [USN:L6N4601BW TEXT:"fell by 11.1 million barrels"] in the week ended October 9, sources said. That was a much bigger draw than [USN:L1N46016I TEXT:"analysts polled"] by Reuters expected.
Official numbers from the US Energy Information Administration are due at 12 p.m. EDT (1600 GMT), delayed by a day following the Columbus Day holiday on Monday.

items.title: TSMC 'prudent' going into 2027 after posting sixth straight quarter of record profit
items.author: Wen-Yee Lee, Ben Blanchard
items.creator: Wen-Yee Lee, Ben Blanchard
items.summary: TSMC, the world's largest manufacturer of advanced chips, struck a note of caution for 2027 on Thursday due to macroeconomic uncertainties, tempering an otherwise upbeat outlook after reporting a sixth consecutive record quarterly profit on robust AI-driven demand.
items.body:
TSMC, the world's largest manufacturer of advanced chips, struck a note of caution for 2027 on Thursday due to macroeconomic uncertainties, tempering an otherwise upbeat outlook after reporting a sixth consecutive record quarterly profit on robust AI-driven demand.
While Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) (2330.TW) said demand was "extremely robust" and it sees no sign of a slowdown in what it calls the AI mega trend, the company was being cautious in its business planning.
"Looking ahead, we continue to observe consumer and price-sensitive end-markets segments are being challenged due to the impact of rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainties," Chief Executive C.C. Wei said on an earnings call. "As such, we are being prudent in our business planning going into 2027."
However, it reiterated that demand far exceeds its supply capacity, with the expectation that its 2026 full-year revenue grows by about 44%, up from a previous forecast of greater than 40% last quarter.
The company also said the emergence of agentic AI central processing units and continued demand for networking chips would drive future silicon demand.
STOCK SHOCK TSMC's results come amid concerns that the AI investment surge is losing momentum. On Wednesday, [USN:L6N4600AA TEXT:"ASML"] (ASML.AS) , the world's largest maker of tools used to make AI chips and advanced semiconductors, provided an upbeat outlook.
TSMC, a key supplier to Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) , said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to rise by as much as 61% from a year earlier to $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. It maintained its capital spending expectation for 2026 at $60 billion to $64 billion.
TSMC's Taipei-listed shares closed down 2% ahead of the earnings release, in line with a broader tech [USN:L6N46104Y TEXT:"sell-off"] amid worries that more interest rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve could pummel shares of AI stocks that are sensitive to higher borrowing costs.
Shares of South Korean rivals Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) slid more than 10%.
Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, which owns TSMC stock, said the company's remarks reflected the caution expressed by many semiconductor companies during recent earnings releases and investor days.
"The key risk is that TSMC's caution translates into broader earnings downgrades across a value chain accustomed to sustained upward revisions, but for now, this looks like sensible expectation management rather than a change in the sector's long-term fundamentals," he added.
Analysts say demand for TSMC's AI chipmaking capacity, as well as its advanced chip packaging technology, CoWoS, remains strong.
That has catapulted Asia's most valuable company to new heights. Its market capitalisation is almost double that of Samsung Electronics at around $2 trillion.
TSMC said net profit in the July-to-September quarter hit T$763.1 billion ($23.59 billion), up 69% from a year earlier and beating a T$746.3 billion LSEG SmartEstimate compiled from 16 analysts.
The result was TSMC's highest-ever quarterly net income, as well as its 11th consecutive quarter of profit growth.
Last week, it reported a 50% year-on-year rise in [USN:L6N45U0AF TEXT:"third-quarter revenue"], beating market forecasts and hitting a new record.
TEXAS EVALUATION TSMC is investing $265 billion to build chip factories in the US state of Arizona, including an additional $100 billion that was unveiled in July.
It said its second fab in Arizona has completed construction, with mass production scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027, ahead of schedule.
In September, Reuters reported that TSMC was [USN:L6N45M06T TEXT:"evaluating"] a potential investment in Texas.
Wei said the company was studying expansion opportunities outside Arizona as major US customers have asked TSMC to increase its local manufacturing capacity, adding that the US government has been supportive.
"Texas is one," Wei said. "We sent teams to Texas to do all the evaluation."
Tesla CEO Elon Musk also said last week that his companies would build and operate the Terafab AI chip complex, with TSMC potentially subleasing a part of it.
Wei said TSMC had discussions with Terafab, but stressed that any fab collaboration would have to be operated by TSMC.
[USN:L6N4600AA TEXT:"ASML"] (ASML.AS) said on Wednesday customers were already looking to place orders for 2029 and 2030, easing concerns that the AI investment boom was losing momentum.
TSMC's Taipei-listed shares have gained 57% so far this year, in line with a 62% rise for the broader Taiwanese market.
($1 = 32.3450 Taiwan dollars)

NEW YORK: Netflix will cut about 1,000 jobs, or 6 per cent of its workforce, US media reported on Wednesday (Oct 14), as the streaming platform experiences slower growth.
When contacted by AFP, the company did not immediately respond.
"Our mission - to entertain the world - is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people and resources," co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters wrote in an internal memo, according to several US media outlets.
Now firmly established at the top of the video streaming market, Netflix is no longer able to grow at the same pace as before.

Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room, the Vatican said.

Pope Leo arrives at Gemelli Hospital ahead of the pontiff's surgery to remove a lung nodule in Rome, Italy, on Oct 13, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Guglielmo Mangiapane)

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo 's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday (Oct 14), after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for lung cancer .
World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Pope Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday.
Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy.
The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness.

Pope Leo normally follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17 and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip.
However, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said on Wednesday that the dates could change because of the amount of time his recovery would take.
The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world 's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.

PRAYERS FOR POPE LEO A prayer was recited for Pope Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery.
The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer , and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancer ous tissue.
Human lung s have five lobes - three in the right lung and two in the left.
The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope 's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone, said late on Tuesday.
The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis.
Dr Serena Ricciardi, a lung cancer specialist at Rome's San Camillo Forlanini Hospital, said that if the cancer had not spread to Pope Leo 's lymph nodes, the surgery may have been sufficient for treatment.
"If there are no further issues or lymph node involvement, we could consider the surgery curative," she told Reuters. "The disease has been completely removed."
Pope Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had recent health issues.

Related:

What we know about Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo recovering after lung cancer operation

ENGAGEMENTS CANCELLED UNTIL NEXT WEEK The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until Oct 20.
The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act of an assembly of bishops called by Pope Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders so far during this papacy.
Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle led the service in place of Pope Leo . The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role.
Political leaders offered messages of support.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope , an American who was born in Chicago.
"May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," he said on X. Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican in May.
There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope , or from Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic.

items.title: Even ASML's strong earnings can't save it! U.S. chip stocks' slump intensifies, with industry index at risk of losing a trillion dollars in market value
items.author: 华尔街见闻
items.creator: 华尔街见闻
items.summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell more than 4% intraday on Wednesday, heading for a six-day losing streak, which would mark its longest losing streak in nearly 17 months. Over the past six days, more than half of the index’s components have fallen at least 10%. ASML is positioned upstream in the semiconductor industry chain. Although strong demand for its lithography equipment indicates that chip manufacturers are still planning capacity expansion, it does not directly prove that the downstream customers of these chip makers will continue to purchase chips at the same pace. While the AI-driven rally has yet to be disproved, the market is raising the threshold for returns.
items.body: The chip stock sell-off, which had just eased during Tuesday's session, intensified again on Wednesday. Memory chip stocks such as Micron Technology and SK hynix weakened once more, and the industry benchmark Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) once fell by over 4% intraday, set to mark its sixth consecutive day of losses. Media outlets report that with concerns mounting over rising interest rates, high valuations, and the costly buildout of AI infrastructure, the total market capitalization of SOX components faces the risk of evaporating by more than $1 trillion. As of Wednesday, June 14 (U.S. Eastern time), when SOX fell over 3% intraday, the index had accumulated a six-day decline of 10%, with over half of its constituents dropping at least 10% over the period. This correction is evolving from short-term profit-taking into a comprehensive test of the AI investment thesis. September’s U.S. CPI inflation was stronger than expected, reinforcing market anxiety about further Fed hikes. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan earlier warned the AI industry could face funding constraints. Even strong results and upgraded sales guidance from semiconductor equipment leader ASML failed to effectively lift chip stocks. The real question now is not merely whether AI demand remains robust, but whether massive capital expenditures can translate into sustainable earnings growth, and whether current valuations have already priced in future profits. SOX Faces Six-Day Losing Streak, Global Chip Stocks Risk Nearly $1 Trillion in Lost Market Value During Wednesday's session, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index hit fresh intraday lows with a drop close to 4.2%, on track to close down for the sixth straight session—marking the longest losing streak since May 2025. At the individual stock level, the correction has spread from memory chips to chip design and manufacturing equipment. According to Bloomberg, over half of SOX constituents have dropped at least 10% in the last six trading days. Arm's U.S. shares (ARM) have fallen nearly 20% over the same period, Applied Materials (AMAT) about 15%, Intel (INTC) approximately 11%. GlobalFoundries (GFS) is the only constituent to post a gain during this timeframe. On Wednesday, Arm plunged over 6% intraday, Intel over 4.6%. Memory stocks, after a brief respite on Tuesday, weakened collectively again: SK hynix's U.S. shares (SKHY) fell over 5.8%, SanDisk (SNDK) dropped 4.9%, Micron Technology (MU) lost 3.5%, and both Western Digital (WDC) and Seagate Technology (STX) slumped over 3% intraday. From Korea and Japan to the U.S., memory chip stocks have already seen severe corrections, and now the decline is spreading further into chip design and equipment manufacturers, showing that investors are reducing exposure across the semiconductor sector. Bloomberg notes that, based on recent declines, SOX constituents are at risk of losing over $1 trillion in market value. This does not mean all that value has already vanished, but rather that if the sell-off continues, the global semiconductor industry may face a dramatic valuation retracement. Rising Inflation, Rate Hike Fears Rekindled, AI High Valuations Under Pressure One major factor fueling the continued chip stock decline is a tightening macro interest rate environment. U.S. September inflation data beat market expectations, with consumer price increases at their highest since April, largely driven by higher fuel costs. This reinforced expectations that the Fed may keep hiking rates, and even if the Fed holds steady later this month, investor perceptions about the future rate path have shifted. For high-valuation tech stocks whose earnings outlook depends on future growth, rising rates mean lower discounted future cash flows and higher costs for financing and expansion. Semiconductor firms, benefiting from AI infrastructure buildout but facing heavy capital expenditure and lengthy payback periods, are especially sensitive to rate changes. Meanwhile, the AI trade itself is under renewed scrutiny. Earlier this week, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan likened some AI fever investors to casino gamblers and warned the industry could face funding constraints—further fueling concerns about the sustainability of the AI investment boom. In recent years, investors have been willing to pay premiums for rapid computing power demand growth; now, the market is taking a harder look at companies’ financing abilities, capex size, and the speed at which profits actually materialize. When inflation pushes up rate expectations, capital costs rise, and valuation pressures mount, even strong long-term demand can’t prevent severe stock price corrections. ASML’s Strong Results—Why Can’t They Save Chip Stocks? This week, as chip stocks fell further, semiconductor equipment titan ASML reported robust quarterly results and raised its full-year sales guidance, with strong multi-year equipment demand from customers. Yet, the earnings report failed to reverse the broader chip stock downturn. Barron's analysis points out that a key reason is that ASML sits upstream in the semiconductor supply chain. Strong demand for its lithography equipment shows that chipmakers are still planning to expand capacity, but doesn't directly prove that downstream chip buyers will keep purchasing at the same pace. ASML’s customers include chipmakers like TSMC and Intel, while the real drivers of the current AI investment cycle are end customers such as Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and other hyperscale data center operators. For chipmakers, equipment orders and long-term capacity planning matter, but more direct impacts on revenue and profits come from whether downstream buyers keep ordering chips—and whether those purchases yield enough returns. ASML's strong performance demonstrates ongoing resilience in AI-related equipment demand, but that alone doesn't dispel market worries about capex efficiency in AI. In other words, order visibility for equipment makers and profit realization for chipmakers are not the same thing. Furthermore, strong demand for ASML’s equipment could have another effect: if tight supply pushes up ASML’s product prices, customers like TSMC and Intel may face higher equipment procurement costs in the future. For companies already facing massive investments to build advanced process capacity, this could further heighten capex pressure. Therefore, ASML’s results failing to lift the whole chip sector doesn’t necessarily mean AI demand is weakening, but rather reflects a market now wanting to see proof that the entire value chain can sustainably profit from AI investment—not just upstream order growth. Wall Street Cuts Outlook: AI Investment to Shift from Spending to Profits Ulrich Hofmann-Burchardi, from UBS Chief Investment Office, noted in a Wednesday research report that pressure on global chip stocks continues to mount. She believes intensifying AI competition, growing funding needs, and rising interest rates could amplify volatility at times, but this correction is more a market expectations reset than a collapse of the AI investment case. This judgment highlights a current market divide: on one hand, AI infrastructure buildout could last for years; on the other, investors are doubting whether this surge in capital spending is sustainable and whether the resulting profits will meet previously lofty projections. Bloomberg points to an upcoming important test: Anthropic’s investor event, reportedly held in San Francisco on Wednesday. Wall Street hopes the AI company will reveal revenue run rates, to better assess if AI company income growth can sustain ever-expanding computing investment. UBS recommends investors focus on whether AI spending can deliver sustainable profit growth, and whether AI applications on the enterprise and consumer sides keep widening. Compared to simply tracking capex totals, these metrics better help determine if today’s investment fever yields stable commercial returns. If AI firms can keep growing revenue and profitability—and prove that huge infrastructure outlays deliver reasonable returns—then the present correction is more likely a recalibration of valuations and expectations. Conversely, if spending outpaces revenue and cash flow improvement, market tolerance for high valuations could fall further. AI Boom Not Disproved, but the Market Is Raising Return Thresholds From SOX’s losing streak, to ASML’s stout earnings failing to spark a rebound, to inflation and rate expectations weighing afresh, today’s chip stock landscape signals investors are shifting from chasing AI-driven growth to scrutinizing real economic returns from AI investment. This doesn’t mean AI demand has collapsed. ASML's orders and sales guidance still show strong semiconductor equipment resilience. Yet, for chip manufacturers and AI infrastructure firms, the market wants more solid proof that ever-increasing capex will translate into matching income, profits, and cash flow. In this context, over $1 trillion in potential market cap at risk reflects not only the scale of recent sell-offs, but also a change in market pricing logic: AI may remain a powerful long-term growth driver, but companies can no longer rely solely on a growth story to fetch premium valuations. Going forward, key variables for chip stocks stabilizing will include AI companies’ revenue run rates, return on capital spending, and their financing capacity in a higher-rate environment.

items.title: BofA's mega-fine blunted by Team Trump history
items.author: Stephen Gandel
items.creator: Stephen Gandel
items.summary: A $1.2 bln penalty over compliance issues often rattles bank boards and shareholders. Just ask erstwhile CEOs of Citi, TD and Wells Fargo. Boss Brian Moynihan's money-laundering mess leaves him in comparatively tepid water, given the administration's vexing signals on wrongdoing.
items.body:
Aesop's "Boy Who Cried Wolf" will be a treasured tale for Bank of America (BAC.N) CEO Brian Moynihan. The mega-lender he runs just copped to violating the Bank Secrecy Act with a deficient anti-money-laundering program, transgressions that include a $1.2 billion fine. Compliance matters of this magnitude tend to unnerve boards and shareholders, but the Trump administration's past pronouncements on financial wrongdoing dilute the moral of this particular story.
The US Treasury Department and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency unveiled enforcement action on Tuesday, accusing BofA of failing to report more than $5 billion of suspicious transactions in a timely manner. The agencies levied one of their biggest-ever penalties because, they said, Moynihan and his team put revenue ahead of addressing concerns raised by regulators before. BofA said it is [USN:O8N43T02A TEXT:""far along with and committed to completing""] the related issues and already absorbed many of the costs, including hundreds of millions of dollars during the third quarter.
Moynihan has some damage control to do, but he may be in relatively tepid water compared to erstwhile counterparts. Citigroup's (C.N) Michael Corbat, Wells Fargo's John Stumpf (WFC.N) and TD Bank's Bharat Masrani (TD.TO) all left their respective CEO roles after running into similarly significant regulatory problems. President Donald Trump's vexing track record, however, probably gives Moynihan extra wiggle room.
It's easy to question the motivations here. For one thing, Trump [USN:FWN3W42W4 TEXT:"pardoned"] Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who had pleaded guilty to anti-money-laundering violations and stepped down from the cryptocurrency exchange as part of a $4.3 billion settlement. Administration officials also have been echoing industry complaints that suspicious-activity reporting rules have become overly burdensome. Dubious probes like the one into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell have more than a whiff of political bullying. Moreover, just days into his second term, the president publicly [USN:S0N3OG012 TEXT:"rebuked"] Moynihan at the World Economic Forum in Davos for allegedly discriminating against conservative customers.
Moynihan is under some justified pressure. BofA's share price gains have broadly under-performed the industry in recent years, prompting investors to push him to boost returns on tangible common equity into the high teens, even as some rivals already exceed 20%. The bank recently tried to [USN:L1N45V0WY TEXT:"reassure"] staff about deal-maker defections, Reuters reported this week. Even excluding the latest regulatory penalty, its third-quarter earnings would have declined, making it an outlier among large lenders.
Although compliance shortcomings add to the CEO's challenges, the true extent of the problem is hard to discern because of who's shouting about them. As a result, Moynihan has scope to keep the real wolves at bay.
Follow Stephen Gandel on LinkedIn and X .
Bank of America on October 13 agreed to pay a $1.2 billion fine to settle accusations in a civil case brought by the financial crimes unit of the Treasury Department and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency that it failed to address previously flagged lapses in its anti-money-laundering controls.
The US regulators said the bank failed to report in a timely way more than $5 billion of suspicious transactions to Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. As part of the settlement, BofA admits that it willfully violated the Bank Secrecy Act and failed to implement and maintain an anti-money-laundering program that met minimum regulatory requirements, Treasury said in a statement.
BofA is required to work with a third party to identify and report suspicious transactions that were undetected and undergo an independent review of its suspicious activity monitoring and other programs, according to the consent order.

US inflation heats up in September; Fed rate hike this month back on table

US inflation rose to 3.7 per cent in September, driven by higher gasoline prices, increasing pressure on households and complicating the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates.

A motorist fills up his tank at a gas station amid a fuel shortage in Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia, Wednesday, Oct 14, 2026. (Photo: AP/Firdia Lisnawati)

WASHINGTON: US consumer prices accele rate d in September as the cost of gasoline surged, dealing another blow to US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections and putting an interest rate increase later this month back on the radar.
The Consumer Price Index report from the Labour Department on Wednesday (Oct 14) showed a broadening of price pressures beyond energy, raising concerns among economists that underlying inflation could be getting sticky. Financial markets now see the Fed eral Reserve's interest rate decision this month as a closer call than before the data was released.
The report added to surveys this month that showed a further deterioration in consumer sentiment and a plunge in Trump's approval rating, driven by angst over the rising cost of living. A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed about 78 per cent of Americans blamed Trump's policies, including tariffs on imports and the Middle East conflict, for rising prices, which are outpacing wages.
"The inflation we're experiencing right now is largely the result of erratic policy from the executive branch," said Kyle Moore, chief economist at the Century Foundation, a progressive think tank.
